A.explanation: Force $F = qE$ is the same because charge $q = Ze$ is the same, but mass differs so acceleration $a = F/m$ differs.

B.explanation: Isotopes have the same proton number $Z$ but different neutron numbers, so neutron number differs.

C.explanation: Total nucleons $A = Z + N$ differs because the neutron number $N$ differs.

D.explanation: Same element means same proton number $Z$, so an uncharged atom with $Z$ electrons has the same electron number.

hints: Notice the phrase isotopes of the same element - recall what proton number $Z$ and neutron number $N$ are the same or different for.
Connect same $Z$ to nuclear charge $Ze$ and to electron number in an uncharged atom, and different $N$ to different mass.
Compare force $F = qE$ with acceleration $a = F/m$ in the same uniform electric field to see why same force does not mean same acceleration.
walkthrough: Recall the definition of isotopes: nuclei with the same proton number $Z$ but different neutron numbers $N$.
Same $Z$ means same nuclear charge $Ze$ and same chemical element, while different $N$ means different nucleon number $A = Z + N$ and different mass.
In the same uniform electric field $E$, the electric force $F = ZeE$ is the same, but acceleration $a = F/m$ is smaller for the heavier isotope, so the accelerations differ.
Therefore same neutrons and same nucleons are both false, because $N$ and $A$ differ between isotopes.
For an uncharged atom, number of electrons equals number of protons $Z$, which is identical for both isotopes. This is option D.
